[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

{{Estimated Date}}

== Biography ==
'''William Glasgow''' was an adult member of the Larne and
Kilwaughter Presbyterian congregation by 1739/40.

The congregation's session accounts record William handling money
received from use of the mortcloth on 17 February 1739/40, in
October 1741 and on 29 December 1743.[https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184109/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/TheirStory2.html]

These entries cannot concern [[Glasgow-3326|William Glasgow]], born
in 1730, who was only about nine to thirteen years old. They establish
that a separate, older William Glasgow was present in the Larne
congregation.

William's date of birth is unknown. A compiled family reconstruction
associates him with a St Cedma's gravestone and gives a birth year of
about 1708. The same reconstruction elsewhere reports conflicting
tombstone-derived years of 1699 and 1708. No photograph or complete
transcription of the memorial has yet been inspected.

A probate index contains an entry for '''William Glasgow of Larne'''
in 1783. This record cannot presently be assigned securely to this
William because the younger William born in 1730 was also an adult
in the Larne area. The year 1783 should not therefore be treated as
This William's proved death year.

The compiled reconstruction implies that William had an eldest son
named '''James'''. It does not provide a baptism, date, mother's name,
will, deed or complete gravestone inscription identifying that son.
James may remain attached as an uncertain child and working hypothesis.
Given the estimated dates, a grandson or later descendant may be more
likely than a direct son; the attachment must not be presented as proved.

The reconstruction is internally inconsistent concerning a later
James Glasgow born about 1775. Its numbered family list places that
James on the same gravestone as the William born in 1730, rather than
This older William. The shared memorial does not itself establish a
father-and-son relationship.

No inspected contemporary record currently identifies William's wife.

William has been described as a son of [[Glasgow-1502|Robert Glasgow]]
and a brother of [[Glasgow-1504|James Glasgow]]. No inspected baptism,
will, deed, marriage settlement or gravestone transcription proves
either relationship. His description as an uncle of James's son
William is consequently also uncertain.


=== Larne leases and later proof of execution ===

A Registry of Deeds memorial records a lease dated 10 March 1736 from the Earl of Antrim to William Glasgow and [[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]] of Larne for two tenements in Newtown of Larne. The lease names no relationship between William and Hugh. Its measuring lives were members of the royal family rather than members of the Glasgow family.<ref name="ROD1736">Registry of Deeds, memorial 63221, lease dated 10 March 1736, Earl of Antrim to William and Hugh Glasgow of Larne; registered 10 April 1738. Original image inspected 21 September 2026. [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSN1-FXR2 FamilySearch image].</ref>

A separate Earl of Antrim lease made in 1737 names William Glasgow of Larne as tenant of a house and garden in Old Town of Larne, on the north side of the street leading from Newtown toward the mill.<ref name="ROD1737">Registry of Deeds, memorial of Earl of Antrim lease to William Glasgow of Larne, made in 1737 and registered in 1739. [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-S3FM-8 FamilySearch image]. The automated transcript obscures part of the original date, so the image should be checked before publishing a verbatim transcription.</ref>

Most importantly, William Glasgow of Larne, described as a gentleman, witnessed a deed dated 19 April 1744 and personally proved its execution at Larne on 6 January 1775.<ref name="ROD1744">Registry of Deeds, memorial of deed dated 19 April 1744, with affidavit of William Glasgow at Larne on 6 January 1775. [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-C674 FamilySearch image].</ref> This directly carries an adult William of Larne from 1744 to 1775. It is much more consistent with this older William than with [[Glasgow-3326|William Glasgow]], reportedly born in 1730 and therefore only about fourteen in 1744. None of these deeds identifies William's parents, wife or children.

=== Joint lessors named in a 1757 assignment ===

A deed poll dated 4 June 1757, Matthew Stewart of Carncastle, farmer, to Robert Rainey of Larne, weaver, concerned a conditional assignment for £20 of Stewart's interest in a lease granted by [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]] of Larne. The original memorial does not date their head lease or describe the holding sufficiently to identify it with the 1736 Newtown tenements.<ref name="JointLessors1757">Registry of Deeds, memorial 159181, manuscript pp. 473–474, deed dated 4 June 1757, registered 26 May 1761; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJM-MJX4 FamilySearch image 257, opening] and [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJM-MJP6 image 258, continuation], original images inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

The joint names and Larne locality strongly support association with these lessees, but the record names no Glasgow relative or relationship between William and Hugh. Neither Glasgow executed this assignment; its registration in 1761 does not prove that either was then living. The separate 1751 and 1767 endorsements to the 1736 lease remain unexamined and may identify replacement lives.<ref>PRONI D2977/3A/4/81/72A, 1736 William and Hugh Glasgow lease with 1751 and 1767 endorsements; [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/eCatNI_IE/SearchPage.aspx PRONI eCatalogue], catalogue description only.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1502]] is assessed at 29% (uncertain). Robert and William are real adults in the Larne/Kilwaughter congregation and an older Robert can fit William’s estimated generation. No held deed or register names Robert as William’s father; the derivative presumed-brother reconstruction is not independent proof.

Existing child-to-father link assessed from held public evidence; Robert is the older congregation adult, distinct from Robert-1143; his c 1675 birth and proposed sons are estimates/hypotheses.

Next useful test: Inspect MIC/1B/6 and early William lease recitals for an explicit parent or family link.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-1505 Classon Porter, “Congregational Memoirs—Larne and Kilwaughter,” The Christian Unitarian, vols. 2–3 (1863–1864), transcript of the congregational records for 1699–1700.]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


=== Preferred father of the Larne ropemaker ===
William is retained as an uncertain father alternative for the Larne ropemaker James-1509,27%. Hugh-1499 is now the preferred possible father,52%. The1760 William witness remains positive association evidence with an unresolved identity, not a father clause.

Select Hugh [[Glasgow-1499]] as the preferred possible father of James [[Glasgow-1509]], the older Belfast/Larne ropemaker, at 52% subjective confidence, replacing William [[Glasgow-1505]] in the local working tree. The archived chronology explicitly places a James, son of Hugh, at New Town/Larne in 1737 and identifies its reported 1762 Janet Shutter groom with that James. Hugh is an independently documented Larne merchant and elder, jointly leasing Newtown property in1736 and dealing with Hugh Shutter in the original1749 mortgage. The later James/Janet account and the distinctive Jane Shutter name in the younger William’s monument fit a recurring Glasgow–Shutter network. These combined named-parent, locality, generation and family-association clues favour Hugh over retaining a William father without a named-son record.

This is a preferred working identification, not a proved father clause for the adult ropemaker. The chronology is one derivative reconstruction: its1737 child,1762 groom and reported1737–1802 stone must not be counted as three independent confirmations. The adult’s1737 birth may itself derive from that reconstruction; the independent1773 affidavit establishes only birth before27 October1743. The original1737 entry,1762 marriage and alleged James/Janet stone remain uninspected. Hugh Shutter’s relationship to Janet is unknown, and a business association does not identify a father-in-law. A different Hugh remains possible. No mother is selected: Ann is not established as the1737 child’s mother by the reviewed account.

The monument’s separately recorded James [[Glasgow-3991]], son of Hugh and Ann, died in1812 aged64 and belongs to the younger1747/48 generation. That is a serious rival explanation: the reported1737 child could have died and the name been used again. It is not a recorded death of that earlier child. Withdraw the categorical earlier inference that the1737 James must have died young. Do not equate the two James profiles, invent a second wife, or infer surviving brothers with the same forename as an established fact. The older ropemaker was already an adult in1760–1761 and over thirty in1773, so he remains distinct from the younger monument/tanner comparison.

Retain William [[Glasgow-1505]] as an unselected uncertain father alternative at27%, preserving his earlier possible but individually unrated placement. A William Glasgow, Larne merchant, witnessed the1760 ropewalk lease, which is genuine positive association with James; the witness is not expressly called his father and may be the older William or another adult namesake. William and Hugh’s joint1736/1757 property activity makes a wider family or business relationship plausible without choosing its degree. William could be father, uncle or another associate. The specific reported Hugh-son identification and Hugh–Shutter connection now favour Hugh, but do not exclude William. The percentages express comparative research judgment, not a measured frequency or independent-source calculation.

One selected father is replaced locally. The child-side working branch contains49 retained pre-1850 profile accounts, including James and uncertain descendants; their own grades are unchanged. This is not49 new or proved relationships. The men were already in the same working component, so no component merger or new genealogical connection is claimed. No vital date, place, spouse, mother, identity merge or live WikiTree field changes. Hugh’s own uncertain ancestry and James’s Inishrush descendants retain their prior assessments.

The next discriminators are the original1737 entry,1762 marriage, full James/Janet monument and any surviving1737-child death or later household recital. The1760 William witness must be identified separately rather than silently assigned to the older William. A document naming a parent, sibling or inherited holding would test the preferred model; its absence is not an automatic exclusion.<ref name="LarnePreferredFather">[https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/Timeline.html Donna Jean Glasgow, Life’s Weaving, archived Kilwaughter/Larne chronology, 1737 and1762 entries; reread18 October2026; derivative reconstruction, original register and reported stone not inspected]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-7XCG Registry of Deeds memorial97407, mortgage6 November1749, FamilySearch image449; original reading of21 September2026 reused]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-S7XZ-8 Registry of Deeds,10 September1760 Gardenmore ropewalk lease, registered24 November1763; maintained original reading reused]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-M72W-M Registry affidavit27 October1773, registered15 November: James of Larne aged upwards of thirty; maintained original reading reused]; [https://archive.org/details/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/page/47/mode/1up Bigger and Hughes, Larne churchyard inscriptions, Ulster Journal of Archaeology, second series6, pp.47–48; previously inspected published monument transcription reused].</ref>


The early session-account dates include:

* adult by 17 February 1739/40;
* living on 29 December 1743.

The dates about 1708 and 1783 should remain uncertain until the full
St Cedma's inscription or another direct record is examined.

The Larne and Kilwaughter Presbyterian collection at PRONI,
reference MIC/1B/6, includes baptisms from 1720 to 1769, marriages
from 1721 to 1769, session minutes and poor accounts. These records
should be searched for:

* a marriage of William Glasgow between approximately 1725 and 1740;
* baptisms of children of William Glasgow;
* a son James;
* any entry naming William's wife;
* references distinguishing the older William from William born
  in 1730.

== Possible Descendants ==

The precise identity of William's children has not been established from
an inspected baptism, will or deed. A plausible descendant reconstruction
can nevertheless be formed from Larne occupational, gravestone and family
naming evidence.

A possible son was '''James Glasgow''', a ropemaker who was already an
adult by 1760/61. An advertisement in the Belfast News-Letter of
2 January 1761 announced that “James Glasgow, Rope maker from Belfast”
had erected a ropewalk at Larne.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 2 January 1761,
advertisement by James Glasgow, ropemaker.</ref>

A compiled family chronology reports that James married '''Janet Shutter'''
in 1762 and had a son William about 1763.<ref>
[https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/Timeline.html
Chronology of the Glasgow family in Northern Ireland].
</ref>

Alexander Holmes's will, dated 5 June 1799, refers to a field held with
James Glasgow and to houses occupied by “James Glasgow, Roper” in Old
Town, Larne.<ref>Registry of Deeds Abstracts of Wills, vol. III,
abstract of the will of Alexander Holmes of Larne, dated 5 June 1799;
RD 527/136/345729; PRONI T681, p.344.</ref>

No inspected record presently names the ropemaker's father. His age,
occupation and location make him a possible son of this William, but the
relationship remains uncertain.

The ropemaker's probable son was '''William Glasgow''', born about 1763
and died 5 October 1816. A published transcription of his gravestone in
Larne Parish Churchyard records his wife Elizabeth and daughters Jane
Shutter, Eliza and Mary.<ref>Francis Joseph Bigger and Herbert Hughes,
“Armorial Sculptured Stones of the County Antrim,” ''Ulster Journal of
Archaeology'', vol. VI (1900), p.47.</ref>

The inscription records:

* Jane Shutter Glasgow, died 21 April 1799 aged nine months;
* William Glasgow, died 5 October 1816 aged 53;
* his wife Elizabeth, died 17 September 1832 aged 60;
* their daughter Eliza, died 25 April 1839 aged 37; and
* their daughter Mary, died 18 October 1844 aged 37.

The name '''Jane Shutter Glasgow''' provides significant evidence that
William was connected with James Glasgow and Janet Shutter. The compiled
chronology identifies William's wife as Elizabeth Stewart of Corran and
records a daughter Elizabeth on 30 August 1802. This daughter may have
been the Eliza named on the gravestone.

James Glasgow, born about 1773/75 and currently attached as William's
uncertain son, may instead have belonged to this later generation. If
The ropemaker James was William's son, James born about 1773/75 would
probably have been William's grandson. The existing uncertain attachment
is retained as a working hypothesis pending identification of the
reported shared gravestone or another family record.

The chronology's identification of the ropemaker as a son of Hugh Glasgow
appears problematic. A published transcription of Hugh's family stone
records his son James as dying on 14 April 1812 aged 64, implying birth
about 1748. He would have been too young to establish the ropewalk in
1761 or marry in 1762. The chronology may therefore have combined two
different men named James Glasgow.

== Research Notes: Parentage and Larne Associations ==

William's parentage has not been proved. The present attachment to Robert
Glasgow is derived from the existing family tree; no inspected baptism, will,
deed or congregational minute names Robert as William's father.

A published transcript of the Larne and Kilwaughter congregational accounts
records that in 1734 the congregation's mortcloth or funeral pall was lodged
with “William Glasgow Major”. Accounts relating to the pall continued until
1759. This is a plausible early occurrence of the present William, although
The entry names no relatives and does not by itself establish identity.<ref>
Classon Porter, “Congregational Memoirs—Larne and Kilwaughter,”
''The Christian Unitarian'', vol. 3 (1864), p. 230.</ref>

Registry of Deeds memorial 62131, concerning a deed dated 10 March 1736,
describes William Glasgow as an adjoining occupier at Larne.<ref>Registry of
Deeds, memorial 62131, vol. 84, p. 481, deed dated 10 March 1736.</ref>

A separate Earl of Antrim lease from March 1736 leased New Town of Larne
tenements jointly to William Glasgow and Hugh Glasgow, both of Larne.<ref>
Registry of Deeds, memorial 63221; PRONI D300/2/1/100/3A-B.</ref> Related
lease endorsements survive under PRONI D2977/3A/4/81/72A. The joint tenancy
proves a close property association but does not state that William and Hugh
were brothers.

The surviving congregational extracts for 1699–1700 distinguish John Glasgow
senior of Kilwaughter, Robert Glasgow of the South Side and James Glasgow,
who was appointed overseer for Kilwaughter. No family relationship between
these men is stated.<ref>Classon Porter, “Congregational Memoirs—Larne and
Kilwaughter,” ''The Christian Unitarian'', vols. 2–3 (1863–1864),
transcript of the congregational records for 1699–1700.</ref>

The Connor diocesan probate index records William Glasgow of Larne in 1783. This is a possible match, not a secure identification: more than one adult William Glasgow was associated with Larne. PRONI reports that the original documents do not survive; the index supplies no relatives or exact death date. The estate year must not be treated as this William's proved death year.<ref>[https://apps.proni.gov.uk/ProniNames_IE/SearchPage.aspx PRONI Name Search], Connor diocesan probate index, William Glasgow, Larne, 1783.</ref>

Hugh, James, William and the younger Robert Glasgow should therefore be
treated as members of an East Antrim research cluster rather than proved
siblings unless a direct relationship record is found.

=== Unidentified William Glasgow, deed witness in 1772 ===
A lease dated 12 May 1772 from John Miller, currier of Gardenmore in Old Town of Larne, to David Drennan, weaver, names Wm Glasgow, David Dickey and James Fairies, all of Larne, as witnesses. Either [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]] or [[Glasgow-3326|William Glasgow]] could be this witness; the deed gives no age, occupation or relative to distinguish them. The son William named in the trust clause is Drennan's son, not a Glasgow relationship. Registration on 9 November 1784 does not prove that the witness William Glasgow was still alive then.<ref>Registry of Deeds, Miller to Drennan, lease 12 May 1772, registered 9 November 1784, manuscript p. 315, image 166; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-SQLT-3 original image], inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

=== Possible Captain Glasgow, vessel William at New-York, 1758 ===
A February 1758 shipping report lists the vessel William, master Glasgow, from London, at New-York.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/34419759/ The Public Advertiser, 1758-02-18, p.1].</ref>

William is the vessel’s name; the master’s personal forename is not stated. The voyage does not identify his residence, birthplace or family.

This may concern [[Glasgow-1505]]. Estimated c.1708/1783 Larne lifespan permits an adult in 1758. William is this candidate’s name, not a forename established by the vessel; no individual voyage connection.

=== Possible William Glascoe / Glascow, 1760 defendant ===
William Glascoe is among prisoners reported sentenced to transportation after Old Bailey trials, for stealing a sack of malt from a warehouse, valued in the newspaper at £4 10s.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/35690357/ Public Ledger or Daily Register of Commerce and Intelligence, 1760-04-18, p.2].</ref>

The newspaper uses Glascoe; the associated Old Bailey case uses Glascow. The case association does not establish the defendant’s origin, family or identity with the later Maryland man.

This may concern [[Glasgow-1505]]. The recorded c. 1708 birth at County Antrim, Ireland is chronologically compatible. The newspaper gives no family or individual identifier connecting this occurrence to Glasgow-1505.

=== Possible William Glasgow, master of the Lady Forbes ===
William Glasgow is named as master of the Lady Forbes in the Sutton shipping casualty report.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050136699/ The Public Register, or, Freeman's Journal, 1768-01-23, p.2].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395700744/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1768-02-06, p.2].</ref>

The January 1768 report says the rum-carrying Lady Forbes, bound for Waterford, was driven ashore near Sutton and the crew were saved. The ship’s Glasgow home port does not give William’s birthplace. No identity with the later brig William or Falmouth master follows.

This may concern [[Glasgow-1505]]. Older Larne William, estimated birth and death; alive in this period as a working hypothesis. No Lady Forbes connection is established.
